prompt: A vertical 9:16 photograph shot on 35 mm colour-negative film at night in heavy rain, taken from inside the cab of a UK ambulance, a tall box-bodied van: the camera sits just behind and above the driver's seat on the right-hand side, looking forward and down through a tall, nearly upright windscreen beaded with rain, wipers parked at the bottom of the glass. The lower third of the frame is the cab: a broad flat van dashboard in dark grey plastic, a coiled radio handset clipped to the dash, a rugged data terminal on a swivel arm whose screen gives only a soft unreadable blue-white glow, and the driver's forearms in green paramedic sleeves with black nitrile-gloved hands resting on a large, flat-angled steering wheel, knuckles tight. Through the glass, the junction, police line and street from the reference image, seen from the ambulance at its stop line: a few car lengths ahead, a row of white police motorcycles and officers in yellow hi-vis stretched across the wet road, the middle officer holding up one gloved hand to stop us, the yellow box-junction hatching glistening beyond them, the junction empty, a red double-decker bus and a queue of cars held on the right with red brake lights, and far up the road a convoy of dark saloon headlights approaching. Light sources: rows of sodium-orange street lamps haloed in the rain, the police bikes' blue strobes, our own blue roof beacons bouncing off the wet bonnet and the windscreen edges, the terminal's faint glow on the driver's gloves, the convoy's white headlights. Cold teal shadows, orange highlights, visible grain, slight halation round every lamp, rain streaks lit in the air. Natural hands with five fingers each, no readable text, numbers, plates or logos anywhere. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 night photograph on 35 mm colour-negative film, real and unpolished, from high up in the cab of a British ambulance van: the lens is over the right shoulder of the driver, raised well above a car's eye height, angled steeply down through a tall, almost vertical windscreen. A single wiper blade is caught mid-sweep, smearing a clean diagonal arc through the rain on the glass so half the view is sharp and half is broken into blurred droplets. Only a thin strip of dashboard shows along the bottom edge, with the top of a large flattish steering wheel and one green-sleeved gloved hand on it. The police line is very close, almost at our front bumper: the junction, police line and street from the reference image, seen from the ambulance at its stop line, with two white police motorcycles and three officers in yellow hi-vis filling the width of the frame just below the bonnet, one officer looking straight up at the cab with his gloved palm raised flat toward us, rain running off his helmet. Behind them the wet yellow box hatching, the empty junction, a red double-decker and a line of cars waiting on the right, and a convoy's headlights glaring down the road beyond. Lights: sodium-orange street lamps overhead, the motorcycles' blue strobes, our ambulance's own blue beacons washing over the wet bonnet and the officers' reflective jackets, the convoy's white headlights flaring in the wet glass. Teal shadows, orange highlights, heavy grain, halation, rain visible in every light. Natural faces and hands, no readable text, plates, numbers or lettering. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph on grainy 35 mm colour-negative film, rainy London night, taken from further back inside a UK ambulance cab, the camera between and slightly behind the two front seats, high up, so the cab frames the view like a dark box: the edge of the driver's headrest and green-uniformed shoulder on the right, the driver's gloved hands on a big flat-angled wheel, a long flat van dashboard spanning the frame with a radio handset on its clip, and a data terminal on a metal arm whose screen casts an unreadable cyan glow onto the headliner and the driver's sleeve. The windscreen is tall and upright, wipers frozen halfway up, rain gathering in streams. Through it, the junction, police line and street from the reference image, seen from the ambulance at its stop line, a little further off: the line of white police motorcycles and officers in yellow hi-vis spaced across the road half a street ahead, one with a raised glove, the yellow box junction shining wet and empty, a red double-decker bus and held cars on the right with brake lights glowing, and a convoy of headlights coming down the long straight road under the lamps. Light sources: sodium-orange street lamps in a receding row, blue police strobes, our own blue beacons reflecting off the wet bonnet and pulsing faintly across the dashboard, red brake lights, the convoy's white headlights, the terminal's glow inside. Deep teal shadows in the cab, warm orange outside, film grain and halation, raindrops sharp on the glass. Natural hands, no extra fingers, no readable text, plates, signs or logos. Thanks.
